The Stranger - A Poem By Rudyard Kipling

The Stranger within my gate,

He may be true or kind,

But he does not talk my talk–

I cannot feel his mind.

I see the face and the eyes and the mouth,

But not the soul behind.

The men of my own stock,

They may do ill or well,

But they tell the lies I am wanted to,

They are used to the lies I tell;

And we do not need interpreters

When we go to buy or sell.

The Stranger within my gates,

He may be evil or good,

But I cannot tell what powers control–

What reasons sway his mood;

Nor when the Gods of his far-off land

Shall repossess his blood.

The men of my own stock,

Bitter bad they may be,

But, at least, they hear the things I hear,

And see the things I see;

And whatever I think of them and their likes

They think of the likes of me.

This was my father’s belief

And this is also mine:

Let the corn be all one sheaf–

And the grapes be all one vine,

Ere our children’s teeth are set on edge

By bitter bread and wine.

– Rudyard Kipling

Daily Devotional

August 23

4 But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, 5 Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;) 6 And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus: (Ephesians 2:4-6 KJV)

Saying that God “is rich in mercy” is quite an understatement, as none of us ever deserved His mercy and love. Not only has God saved us through His grace, but has given us all spiritual blessing in heavenly places (Ephesians 1:3). What love God has shown to us, to give us so much when we were, and are, so undeserving (1 John 1:8). God has extended His grace to all mankind (Titus 2:11), but not all will be saved, as you must have faith to appropriate the grace. You are saved by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8).

Since we are now one with Christ, (if born again), we truly do sit in heavenly places with Jesus. Since we are in Christ, and Christ is in us (Galatians 4:6), and since Jesus has the whole Godhead in Him, that means we now have the whole Godhead in us. Wow! If you can get your mind wrapped around this fact, you might come to realize that with that power now in us, we might just be able to overcome any sickness, disease or problem that ever comes against us. We not only have the Godhead in us, but we have the devil under our feet (James 4:7), and can just stomp on him when he gives us any trouble. I love to think of doing just that. Thank you Jesus and Father God for all you have done for your children.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
